title: Frobenius coefficient morphisms
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], let $X_0$ be a separated
finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi$ be
the $q$-power scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], with
iterates $\Phi^m$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

1. A *Frobenius coefficient morphism* on $K$ is an arbitrary morphism
$$
\psi:L\Phi^*K\longrightarrow K
$$
in the derived category of $X$; no invertibility is required.
1. Its *iterates* $\psi_m:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$, $m\geq1$, are defined
recursively by $\psi_1=\psi$ and, for $m\geq2$,
$$
\psi_m:\;L\Phi^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
L\Phi^*L\Phi^{(m-1)*}K
\xrightarrow{\ L\Phi^*\psi_{m-1}\ }L\Phi^*K
\xrightarrow{\ \psi\ }K,
$$
where the first arrow is the composition isomorphism of derived
pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $\Phi^m=\Phi^{m-1}\circ\Phi$; thus $\psi_m$ is the
composite of the pulled-back copies $L\Phi^{i*}\psi$,
$0\leq i\leq m-1$, exactly as for the iterated Weil isomorphism of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map].
1. Its *graph map* in degree $m$ is the graph correspondence of
[def-trf-graph-correspondence] attached to $(h,v)=(\Phi^m,\psi_m)$:
$$
c_m=(c_1,c_2)=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m),\qquad u=\psi_m:
Lc_2^*K=L\Phi^{m*}K\longrightarrow K=Rc_1^!K .
$$
1. Its *global operator* in degree $m$ is
$$
F_{c,m}(\psi)=T_{c_m}(\psi_m):R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$
the global operator of [def-trf-global-operator] of the graph map. It
is defined because $\Phi$ is finite by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius],
so the ordinary leg $c_2=\Phi^m$ is finite by repeated application of
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], hence proper by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The exceptional leg
$c_1=\operatorname{id}_X$ is admissible in the constructible sense of
[def-trf-admissibility]; the identity compact-support comparison and
exceptional adjunction of [sk-d-six] identify $Rc_1^!$ with
$\operatorname{id}$. All equalities involving $Rc_1^!K=K$ above are
read through this canonical identity comparison.

*Example.* For a strict Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the scheme-Frobenius map
$u_1=\varphi\circ\kappa_K:L\Phi^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map] is an (invertible) Frobenius coefficient
morphism; the notion above drops the invertibility, and the iterates,
graph map and global operator are given by the same composites.

split_report.summary: Audited this definition against the current blueprint and all seven imported dependencies. Kept the arbitrary (possibly noninvertible) coefficient map, positive recursion, graph and global operator unchanged mathematically. Added existing nodes for derived pullback composition, composition of finite maps, finite implies proper, constructible admissibility and the identity exceptional comparison. No new nodes and no theorem proof are needed for a definition. The upstream WeilComplex data cover part of the item, but coeffIterate_one is sorry and the strict-Weil Galois comparison example is not supplied by those declarations, so no exact attachment is claimed. Second reading clarified that the recursive formula is for m >= 2, independently reran grep and LeanFinder searches, and rechecked every clause against the current blueprint and dependency statements.
split_report.blueprint: Current definition clauses 1–4 and example; unit sk-d-weil paragraphs defining arbitrary coefficient maps, iterates and graph/global operators. sk-d-weil is the broader same-notion interface, not a replacement for the detailed positive recursion and strict-Weil example.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q83-a90fd4b1e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item against main-20261015 sk-d-weil/def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism.md (order 2640). Its text is the same as the master snapshot. The delivery changes no mathematics: it limits the recursion to m>=2 and adds four precise citations, replacing the collector def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties for finite=>proper. Clause 2: lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition (Stacks 0D6D, sites-cohomology.tex l.3658) with h=Phi, k=Phi^(m-1) gives L(Phi^m)^* ≅ LPhi^* L(Phi^(m-1))^* in the stated direction, and the types of LPhi^*psi_(m-1) and then psi check. Clause 3: Phi^m is finite by 01WK (Finite.lean:84), proper by 01WN (Proper.lean:69), hence a separated finite-type k-endomorphism, as def-trf-graph-correspondence requires. Clause 4: def-trf-global-operator needs only proper c_2; id is exceptionally admissible by def-trf-admissibility; R(id)^! ≅ id is the adjoint identity comparison stated in sk-d-six (also prop-functor-package item 3). Example: u_1 = phi∘kappa^(1)_K from def-trf-iterated-weil-map is an invertible psi; the example claims no psi_m = u_m cocycle. Phi is the base-changed q-power scheme Frobenius, kept distinct from g_gamma. The coefficient category is D^b_ctf(X,A) inside D(X_proet,A), and the target is not weakened. Edge cases m=1, m=2, K=0, psi=0, X=Spec k, X empty and nonreduced X_0 all pass. There are no new nodes. The only other definition is sk-d-weil (broader), correctly recorded in same_as.
